method: Independent Python transcription of statically disassembled aPLib-style loader; no original x86 or imported functions executed; decompressed bytes retained only in process memory for hashes.
limitations: This is the first protector-stage destination, not a reconstructed runnable game executable.
Successful bounded decompression does not prove endpoint selection was decoded.
No Windows PE, decrypted game logic, import call, anti-cheat callback or networking code was executed.

implementation_review.result: No defect identified in the bounded decoder implementation.
checks: MSB-first bit tags and per-block reset match DL sentinel behavior.
Gamma branches and literal/short/long/repeated/tiny reference state transitions match the disassembly.
Distance length adjustments match thresholds 0x7f, 0x500 and 0x7d00.
Previous distance and output history persist across block boundaries; overlapping copies advance byte by byte.
Source reads are bounded to the .boot raw section, destination to .winlice virtual capacity; backward references and 32-bit arithmetic are validated.
Every loop has input, arithmetic or operation bounds; an overall 64,000,000-operation budget also applies.
The decoder pins the source build SHA256 and writes derived bytes only under temporary analysis.

bounded_next_entry_static_review.base_setup: Two call/jump/pop sequences compute protector base 0x819000 in EBP and preferred image base 0x400000 in EAX.
bounded_next_entry_static_review.conclusion: The followed path transitions into densely obfuscated stack/register setup and control-flow trampolines. No additional isolated pure byte-transform routine was established in this bounded review.
limitations: The helper region intermixes jump stubs and data; linear decoding between known control-flow targets is not reliable.
Adjacent indirect-call wrappers were observed but not established as part of the followed entry path.
This limited view does not prove that further offline analysis is impossible or that a particular VM/runtime/API is required.
